analysis.title: US EQUITIES - back to panic
key_insights: GS equity derivatives desk (Lee Coppersmith) says the 11/5 vol repricing was extreme. Clients sold protection into Wednesday's post-midterm relief rally, leaving the market underhedged ahead of Thursday's reversal. Equities unwound, hedge funds faced forced liquidations, and there was a scramble to buy back protection that had just been sold.

The desk's Vol Panic Index rose about 5 points to 9.57 out of 10 on 11/5, back in the panic zone (9.5+). That was the 3rd largest daily jump ever, after Wednesday's drop, which was the 4th largest ever. The combined two-day swing was the largest on record.
The 10-day volatility of the Vol Panic Index reached an all-time high. VVIX (the volatility of the VIX) had its 2nd largest one-day increase ever, behind only February 2018 'Volmageddon'.

VIX is in the high 20s. VXN (Nasdaq's VIX) reached its highest level since Liberation Day and had its biggest one-day repricing since Covid. The whole VIX curve flipped from contango to sharp backwardation, which signals more near-term uncertainty.

Cboe traded more than 11mm puts on 11/5, the largest put volume day on record and above the prior high in April 2025. Index puts led. Single-stock put activity was the 4th highest day ever, so most of the demand was broad market protection.

Hedge fund damage on 11/5: Fundamental L/S -1.3% (-2 SD), US funds -1.7%, TMT funds down more than 4%, Multi-Strats -1.4%, Momentum a 3.7 SD move lower. Systematic L/S held up at +0.2%. TMT managers are roughly flat YTD versus +24% before the summer AI unwind.

History after panic: following the prior 15 Vol Panic signals above 9.5, the S&P gained an average 4.6% over 3 months (80% hit rate) and 9.0% over 6 months (73% hit rate). The immediate path has been less reliable while the market is still in price discovery.

The midterms added political and regulatory uncertainty to the AI buildout. Texas is 20%/27% of under-construction US data center additions in 2027/28, and potential moratoriums raise timing and cost concerns. The desk distinguishes delays, which could extend the construction cycle, from cancellations.

GS Research raised its US data center construction spending forecasts to $80bn/$100bn in 2026/27, with $125bn expected in 2028. About $300bn of construction value is under way, and the high-probability pipeline takes that closer to $900bn.

The desk's read is that 11/5 was as much a poor technical setup and forced re-hedging as a fundamental deterioration. Near-term tails remain large and more positioning needs to be worked through. With panic readings at extremes and spending still healthy, the setup looks more interesting as forced selling runs its course, though it is not necessarily a reason to rush back into risk.

sector_views.rationale: Midterm-driven regulatory risk in Texas could delay data center projects, but the desk sees delays extending the cycle rather than cancelling it, with spending visibility through 2028.
